sanskrit: mā yotsīr gurubhiḥ sārdhaṃ balavadbhiś ca pāṇḍava sadṛśais tāta yudhyasva vrīḍāṃ mā kuru pāṇḍava gṛhaṃ vā gaccha mādreya yatra vā kṛṣṇaphalgunau
english: Do not fight against your elders and against the mighty, O Pāṇḍava; fight rather against your equals, my child. Be not ashamed, O Pāṇḍava. Go home, O son of Mādrī, or go to where Kṛṣṇa and Phalguna are.

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja vyasarjayata taṃ tataḥ vadhaprāptaṃ tu taṃ rājan nāvadhīt sūtanandanaḥ smṛtvā kuntyā vaco rājaṃs tata enaṃ vyasarjayat
english: Having spoken thus, O great king, he then let him go. Though that man had come within reach of death, O king, the son of the charioteer did not slay him; remembering the words of Kuntī, O king, he set him free.

sanskrit: visṛṣṭaḥ pāṇḍavo rājan sūtaputreṇa dhanvinā vrīḍann iva jagāmātha yudhiṣṭhirarathaṃ prati
english: Released by the bowman son of the charioteer, the Pāṇḍava, O king, went off as if abashed toward the chariot of Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: āruroha rathaṃ cāpi sūtaputrapratāpitaḥ niḥśvasan duḥkhasaṃtaptaḥ kumbhe kṣipta ivoragaḥ
english: Scorched by the son of the charioteer, he mounted his chariot, sighing and burning with grief, like a serpent flung into a jar.

sanskrit: taṃ visṛjya raṇe karṇaḥ pāñcālāṃs tvarito yayau rathenātipatākena candravarṇahayena ca
english: Having let him go in the battle, Karṇa swiftly advanced upon the Pāñcālas with his chariot of towering banners and moon-white horses.

sanskrit: tatrākrando mahān āsīt pāṇḍavānāṃ viśāṃ pate dṛṣṭvā senāpatiṃ yāntaṃ pāñcālānāṃ rathavrajān
english: At that, O lord of peoples, there arose a great wail among the Pāṇḍavas as they beheld the general advancing upon the ranks of Pāñcāla chariots.

sanskrit: tatrākaron mahārāja kadanaṃ sūtanandanaḥ madhyaṃ gate dinakare cakravat pracaran prabhuḥ
english: There, O great king, the son of the charioteer wrought havoc, that lord ranging like a wheel as the sun reached the midday sky.

sanskrit: bhagnacakrai rathaiḥ ke cic chinnadhvajapatākibhiḥ sasūtair hatasūtaiś ca bhagnākṣaiś caiva māriṣa hriyamāṇān apaśyāma pāñcālānāṃ rathavrajān
english: With wheels shattered, with standards and banners cut down, with their charioteers slain or yet alive, with axles broken, O honored one, we saw the ranks of Pāñcāla chariots being borne away.

sanskrit: tatra tatra ca saṃbhrāntā vicerur mattakuñjarāḥ davāgninā parītāṅgā yathaiva syur mahāvane
english: Here and there, bewildered, the maddened elephants roamed about, their limbs as though encircled by a forest fire in a great wood.

sanskrit: bhinnakumbhā virudhirāś chinnahastāś ca vāraṇāḥ bhinnagātravarāś caiva cchinnavālāś ca māriṣa chinnābhrāṇīva saṃpetur vadhyamānā mahātmanā
english: With their temple-bosses split, streaming blood, their trunks lopped off, their finest limbs gashed and their tails sheared away, O honored one, the elephants, slaughtered by that great-souled one, fell like sundered clouds.

sanskrit: apare trāsitā nāgā nārācaśatatomaraiḥ tam evābhimukhā yānti śalabhā iva pāvakam
english: Other elephants, terrified by hundreds of iron shafts and lances, rushed straight toward him like moths into a flame.

sanskrit: apare niṣṭanantaḥ sma vyadṛśyanta mahādvipāḥ kṣarantaḥ śoṇitaṃ gātrair nagā iva jalaplavam
english: Other great elephants were seen trumpeting in agony, pouring blood from their bodies like mountains streaming with cascades of water.

sanskrit: uraśchadair vimuktāś ca vālabandhaiś ca vājinaḥ rājataiś ca tathā kāṃsyaiḥ sauvarṇaiś caiva bhūṣaṇaiḥ
english: And the horses, stripped of their breast-plates and tail-trappings, and of their ornaments of silver, of bronze, and of gold,

sanskrit: hīnā āstaraṇaiś caiva khalīnaiś ca vivarjitāḥ cāmaraiś ca kuthābhiś ca tūṇīraiḥ patitair api
english: bereft of their saddle-cloths and rid of their bits, deprived of their chowries and housings, with their quivers fallen away,

sanskrit: nihataiḥ sādibhiś caiva śūrair āhavaśobhibhiḥ apaśyāma raṇe tatra bhrāmyamāṇān hayottamān
english: and their riders slain — heroes who had been the splendor of the fight — we saw those splendid horses wandering aimlessly there in the battle.

sanskrit: prāsaiḥ khaḍgaiś ca saṃsyūtān ṛṣṭibhiś ca narādhipa hayayodhān apaśyāma kañcukoṣṇīṣadhāriṇaḥ
english: Pierced through by darts, by swords, and by spears, O lord of men, we saw the cavalrymen, clad in their corselets and turbans.

sanskrit: rathān hemapariṣkārān suyuktāñ javanair hayaiḥ bhramamāṇān apaśyāma hateṣu rathiṣu drutam
english: We saw chariots adorned with gold and well-yoked with swift horses careering wildly about, their warriors slain.

sanskrit: bhagnākṣakūbarān kāṃś cic chinnacakrāṃś ca māriṣa vipatākādhvajāṃś cānyāñ chinneṣāyugabandhurān
english: Some with their axles and shafts broken, some with wheels cut off, O honored one, and others stripped of pennon and standard, with pole, yoke, and seat hewn apart.

sanskrit: vihīnān rathinas tatra dhāvamānān samantataḥ sūryaputraśarais trastān apaśyāma viśāṃ pate
english: There we saw the warriors who had lost their cars running about in every direction, terror-stricken by the arrows of the Sun's son, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: viśastrāṃś ca tathaivānyān saśastrāṃś ca bahūn hatān tāvakāñ jālasaṃchannān uroghaṇṭāvibhūṣitān
english: And we saw others, both weaponless and still bearing arms, slain in great numbers — your own men, sheathed in mail and adorned with breast-bells.

sanskrit: nānāvarṇavicitrābhiḥ patākābhir alaṃkṛtān padātīn anvapaśyāma dhāvamānān samantataḥ
english: We beheld the foot-soldiers, decked with banners gay in many varied hues, running about on every side.

sanskrit: śirāṃsi bāhūn ūrūṃś ca chinnān anyāṃs tathā yudhi karṇacāpacyutair bāṇair apaśyāma vinākṛtān
english: By the arrows loosed from Karṇa's bow we saw still others in the battle, their heads, their arms, and their thighs lopped off, made limbless.

sanskrit: mahān vyatikaro raudro yodhānām anvadṛśyata karṇasāyakanunnānāṃ hatānāṃ niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: A great and terrible carnage of warriors was seen — of men struck down by Karṇa's missiles, slain by his whetted shafts.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare sūtaputreṇa sṛñjayāḥ tam evābhimukhā yānti pataṃgā iva pāvakam
english: The Sṛñjayas, slaughtered in the battle by the son of the charioteer, rushed straight toward him like insects into a flame.

sanskrit: taṃ dahantam anīkāni tatra tatra mahāratham kṣatriyā varjayām āsur yugāntāgnim ivolbaṇam
english: That mighty warrior, burning down the armies here and there, the kṣatriyas shunned as one shuns the raging fire of the world's end.

sanskrit: hataśeṣās tu ye vīrāḥ pāñcālānāṃ mahārathāḥ tān prabhagnān drutān karṇaḥ pṛṣṭhato vikirañ śaraiḥ abhyadhāvata tejasvī viśīrṇakavacadhvajān
english: And those great car-warriors of the Pāñcālas who survived the slaughter — broken and in flight, their armor and standards shattered — Karṇa, blazing with valor, pursued from behind, scattering arrows upon them.

sanskrit: tāpayām āsa tān bāṇaiḥ sūtaputro mahārathaḥ madhyaṃdinam anuprāpto bhūtānīva tamonudaḥ
english: The mighty car-warrior, the son of the charioteer, scorched them with his arrows, as the dispeller of darkness, having reached the noontide, scorches all beings.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yuyutsuṃ tava putraṃ tu prādravantaṃ mahad balam ulūko 'bhyapatat tūrṇaṃ tiṣṭha tiṣṭheti cābravīt
english: Saṃjaya said: As your son Yuyutsu was rushing against the great host, Ulūka swiftly fell upon him, crying, "Stand! Stand!"

sanskrit: yuyutsus tu tato rājañ śitadhāreṇa patriṇā ulūkaṃ tāḍayām āsa vajreṇendra ivācalam
english: Then Yuyutsu, O king, with a sharp-edged feathered shaft struck Ulūka as Indra strikes a mountain with the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: ulūkas tu tataḥ kruddhas tava putrasya saṃyuge kṣurapreṇa dhanuś chittvā tāḍayām āsa karṇinā
english: Thereupon Ulūka, enraged, in the encounter cut your son's bow with a razor-edged arrow and struck him with a barbed shaft.

sanskrit: tad apāsya dhanuś chinnaṃ yuyutsur vegavattaram anyad ādatta sumahac cāpaṃ saṃraktalocanaḥ
english: Casting aside that severed bow, Yuyutsu, his eyes red with rage, took up another very great and more powerful bow.

sanskrit: śākuniṃ ca tataḥ ṣaṣṭyā vivyādha bharatarṣabha sārathiṃ tribhir ānarchat taṃ ca bhūyo vyavidhyata
english: And then, O bull of the Bharatas, he pierced the son of Śakuni with sixty arrows, struck his charioteer with three, and wounded him yet again.

sanskrit: ulūkas taṃ tu viṃśatyā viddhvā hemavibhūṣitaiḥ athāsya samare kruddho dhvajaṃ ciccheda kāñcanam
english: But Ulūka, having pierced him with twenty gold-decked shafts, then in his wrath cut down his golden standard in the battle.

sanskrit: sa cchinnayaṣṭiḥ sumahāñ śīryamāṇo mahādhvajaḥ papāta pramukhe rājan yuyutsoḥ kāñcanojjvalaḥ
english: That great standard, its staff severed and crumbling, blazing with gold, fell before Yuyutsu's eyes, O king.

sanskrit: dhvajam unmathitaṃ dṛṣṭvā yuyutsuḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ ulūkaṃ pañcabhir bāṇair ājaghāna stanāntare
english: Seeing his standard struck down, Yuyutsu, swooning with rage, smote Ulūka in the middle of the breast with five arrows.

sanskrit: ulūkas tasya bhallena tailadhautena māriṣa śiraś ciccheda sahasā yantur bharatasattama
english: With a broad-headed shaft burnished in oil, O honored one, Ulūka instantly struck off the head of his charioteer, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: jaghāna caturo 'śvāṃś ca taṃ ca vivyādha pañcabhiḥ so 'tividdho balavatā pratyapāyād rathāntaram
english: He slew the four horses too and pierced him with five arrows; sorely wounded by the mighty one, Yuyutsu withdrew to another chariot.

sanskrit: taṃ nirjitya raṇe rājann ulūkas tvarito yayau pāñcālān sṛñjayāṃś caiva vinighnan niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Having vanquished him in battle, O king, Ulūka swiftly went on, smiting the Pāñcālas and the Sṛñjayas with his whetted shafts.

sanskrit: śatānīkaṃ mahārāja śrutakarmā sutas tava vyaśvasūtarathaṃ cakre nimeṣārdhād asaṃbhramam
english: Your son Śrutakarman, O great king, in half the twinkling of an eye and without flurry, robbed Śatānīka of horses, charioteer, and car.

sanskrit: hatāśve tu rathe tiṣṭhañ śatānīko mahābalaḥ gadāṃ cikṣepa saṃkruddhas tava putrasya māriṣa
english: Standing in his car whose horses were slain, the mighty Śatānīka, in fury, hurled his mace at your son, O honored one.

sanskrit: sā kṛtvā syandanaṃ bhasma hayāṃś caiva sasārathīn papāta dharaṇīṃ tūrṇaṃ dārayantīva bhārata
english: That mace, reducing the chariot to ashes along with the horses and the charioteer, swiftly fell to earth as if cleaving it open, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau virathau vīrau kurūṇāṃ kīrtivardhanau apākrametāṃ yuddhārtau prekṣamāṇau parasparam
english: Both those heroes, deprived of their chariots, augmenters of the Kurus' glory, withdrew, eager still to fight, gazing upon each other.

sanskrit: putras tu tava saṃbhrānto vivitso ratham āviśat śatānīko 'pi tvaritaḥ prativindhyarathaṃ gataḥ
english: Your son, agitated, mounted the chariot of Vivitsu, while Śatānīka in haste went over to the car of Prativindhya.

sanskrit: sutasomas tu śakuniṃ vivyādha niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ nākampayata saṃrabdho vāryogha iva parvatam
english: Sutasoma, full of fury, pierced Śakuni with his whetted shafts, yet could not shake him, even as a flood of water cannot shake a mountain.

sanskrit: sutasomas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā pitur atyantavairiṇam śarair anekasāhasraiś chādayām āsa bhārata
english: Seeing in him his father's bitterest foe, Sutasoma covered him with many thousands of arrows, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tāñ śarāñ śakunis tūrṇaṃ cicchedānyaiḥ patatribhiḥ laghvastraś citrayodhī ca jitakāśī ca saṃyuge
english: Śakuni swiftly cut down those arrows with other winged shafts — light-handed with his weapons, a brilliant fighter, and ever wearing the look of victory in the fray.

sanskrit: nivārya samare cāpi śarāṃs tān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ ājaghāna susaṃkruddhaḥ sutasomaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Having warded off those arrows in the battle with his whetted shafts, he, exceedingly wroth, struck Sutasoma with three arrows.

sanskrit: tasyāśvān ketanaṃ sūtaṃ tilaśo vyadhamac charaiḥ syālas tava mahāvīryas tatas te cukruśur janāḥ
english: With his arrows your brother-in-law of mighty valor cut that man's horses, banner, and charioteer to pieces; thereupon the people cried out.

sanskrit: hatāśvo virathaś caiva chinnadhanvā ca māriṣa dhanvī dhanurvaraṃ gṛhya rathād bhūmāv atiṣṭhata vyasṛjat sāyakāṃś caiva svarṇapuṅkhāñ śilāśitān
english: His horses slain, his car destroyed, his bow cut, O honored one, the bowman took up another excellent bow and, descending from the chariot, stood upon the ground, and loosed shafts gold-feathered and whetted on stone.

sanskrit: chādayām āsur atha te tava syālasya taṃ ratham pataṃgānām iva vrātāḥ śaravrātā mahāratham
english: Then those flights of arrows covered the car of your brother-in-law, that great warrior, as swarms of insects might cover it.

sanskrit: rathopasthān samīkṣyāpi vivyathe naiva saubalaḥ pramṛdnaṃś ca śarāṃs tāṃs tāñ śaravrātair mahāyaśāḥ
english: Though he saw them descending upon the floor of his car, the son of Subala was not dismayed in the least, but, illustrious one, crushed those arrows with his own showers of shafts.

sanskrit: tatrātuṣyanta yodhāś ca siddhāś cāpi divi sthitāḥ sutasomasya tat karma dṛṣṭvāśraddheyam adbhutam rathasthaṃ nṛpatiṃ taṃ tu padātiḥ sann ayodhayat
english: At this the warriors there, and the perfected beings stationed in the sky, were filled with delight, beholding that incredible and wondrous feat of Sutasoma — that, himself on foot, he gave battle to that prince who stood upon his car.

sanskrit: tasya tīkṣṇair mahāvegair bhallaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ vyahanat kārmukaṃ rājā tūṇīraṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ
english: With keen, swift, smooth-jointed broad-headed shafts the prince utterly shattered his bow and his quiver as well.

sanskrit: sa cchinnadhanvā samare khaḍgam udyamya nānadan vaiḍūryotpalavarṇābhaṃ hastidantamayatsarum
english: His bow cut, he in the battle, roaring aloud, raised on high a sword the hue of lapis and the blue lotus, its hilt fashioned of ivory.

sanskrit: bhrāmyamāṇaṃ tatas taṃ tu vimalāmbbaravarcasam kālopamaṃ tato mene sutasomasya dhīmataḥ
english: As wise Sutasoma whirled that blade, gleaming like the cloudless sky, it seemed then to all like Death himself.

sanskrit: so 'carat sahasā khaḍgī maṇḍalāni sahasraśaḥ caturviṃśan mahārāja śikṣābalasamanvitaḥ
english: Sword in hand, endowed with training and strength, he suddenly moved through circling figures by the thousand — four-and-twenty of them, O great king.

sanskrit: saubalas tu tatas tasya śarāṃś cikṣepa vīryavān tān āpatata evāśu ciccheda paramāsinā
english: Then the valiant son of Subala hurled arrows at him, and those, even as they fell upon him, he swiftly cut apart with his excellent sword.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja saubalaḥ paravīrahā prāhiṇot sutasomasya śarān āśīviṣopamān
english: Then, enraged, O great king, the son of Subala, slayer of hostile heroes, sped at Sutasoma arrows like venomous serpents.

sanskrit: ciccheda tāṃś ca khaḍgena śikṣayā ca balena ca darśayaṃl lāghavaṃ yuddhe tārkṣyavīryasamadyutiḥ
english: These too he cut with his sword, by skill and by strength, displaying his nimbleness in the fight, radiant with valor like Garuḍa.

sanskrit: tasya saṃcarato rājan maṇḍalāvartane tadā kṣurapreṇa sutīkṣṇena khaḍgaṃ ciccheda suprabham
english: As he ranged about, O king, weaving his circling movements, the son of Subala then cut his gleaming sword with a keen razor-edged shaft.

sanskrit: sa cchinnaḥ sahasā bhūmau nipapāta mahān asiḥ avaśasya sthitaṃ haste taṃ khaḍgaṃ satsaruṃ tadā
english: That great sword, severed, fell at once to the ground; only the hilt with a fragment of blade remained, perforce, in his hand.

sanskrit: chinnam ājñāya nistriṃśam avaplutya padāni ṣaṭ prāvidhyata tataḥ śeṣaṃ sutasomo mahārathaḥ
english: Knowing his blade was cut, Sutasoma, that great car-warrior, sprang back six paces and then hurled the remnant at his foe.

sanskrit: sa cchittvā saguṇaṃ cāpaṃ raṇe tasya mahātmanaḥ papāta dharaṇīṃ tūrṇaṃ svarṇavajravibhūṣitaḥ sutasomas tato 'gacchac chrutakīrter mahāratham
english: That fragment, decked with gold and diamond, cut the bowstring and bow of the great-souled foe in the battle and swiftly fell to the earth; thereupon Sutasoma went over to the great chariot of Śrutakīrti.

sanskrit: saubalo 'pi dhanur gṛhya ghoram anyat suduḥsaham abhyayāt pāṇḍavānīkaṃ nighnañ śatrugaṇān bahūn
english: The son of Subala too, taking up another terrible and well-nigh unbearable bow, advanced upon the Pāṇḍava host, slaying many bands of foes.

sanskrit: tatra nādo mahān āsīt pāṇḍavānāṃ viśāṃ pate saubalaṃ samare dṛṣṭvā vicarantam abhītavat
english: At that there arose a great outcry among the Pāṇḍavas, O lord of peoples, as they beheld the son of Subala ranging fearlessly through the battle.

sanskrit: tāny anīkāni dṛptāni śastravanti mahānti ca drāvyamāṇāny adṛśyanta saubalena mahātmanā
english: Those proud and mighty armies, well-armed though they were, were seen put to flight by the great-souled son of Subala.

sanskrit: yathā daityacamūṃ rājan devarājo mamarda ha tathaiva pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ saubaleyo vyanāśayat
english: As the king of the gods once crushed the host of the Daityas, O king, even so did the son of Subala destroy the army of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ kṛpo rājan vārayām āsa saṃyuge yathā dṛptaṃ vane nāgaṃ śarabho vārayed yudhi
english: Kṛpa, O king, checked Dhṛṣṭadyumna in the encounter, as a śarabha in the wild would check a proud elephant in combat.

sanskrit: niruddhaḥ pārṣatas tena gautamena balīyasā padāt padaṃ vicalituṃ nāśaknot tatra bhārata
english: Held in check by that mightier descendant of Gautama, the son of Pṛṣata could not move there even a single step, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: gautamasya vapur dṛṣṭvā dhṛṣṭadyumnarathaṃ prati vitresuḥ sarvabhūtāni kṣayaṃ prāptaṃ ca menire
english: Beholding the form of the descendant of Gautama bearing down upon Dhṛṣṭadyumna's chariot, all beings trembled and deemed that destruction had come.

sanskrit: tatrāvocan vimanaso rathinaḥ sādinas tathā droṇasya nidhane nūnaṃ saṃkruddho dvipadāṃ varaḥ
english: At this the car-warriors and horsemen, downcast in spirit, said: "Surely the best of men is enraged at the slaying of Droṇa."

sanskrit: śāradvato mahātejā divyāstravid udāradhīḥ api svasti bhaved adya dhṛṣṭadyumnasya gautamāt
english: "The son of Śaradvat is of great splendor, knower of celestial weapons, lofty of mind. Will it be well today for Dhṛṣṭadyumna at the hands of this descendant of Gautama?

sanskrit: apīyaṃ vāhinī kṛtsnā mucyeta mahato bhayāt apy ayaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ sarvān na no hanyāt samāgatān
english: Will this whole army be delivered from its great peril? Will this brāhmaṇa not slay us all, assembled here together?"

sanskrit: yādṛśaṃ dṛśyate rūpam antakapratimaṃ bhṛśam gamiṣyaty adya padavīṃ bhāradvājasya saṃyuge
english: "Such is the form he wears, terribly like unto Death, that today in the battle he will follow the path of the son of Bharadvāja."

sanskrit: ācāryaḥ kṣiprahastaś ca vijayī ca sadā yudhi astravān vīryasaṃpannaḥ krodhena ca samanvitaḥ
english: "The preceptor is swift of hand and ever victorious in fight, master of weapons, endowed with valor, and now possessed by wrath."

sanskrit: pārṣataś ca bhṛśaṃ yuddhe vimukho 'dyāpi lakṣyate ity evaṃ vividhā vācas tāvakānāṃ paraiḥ saha
english: "And the son of Pṛṣata is even now seen sorely averse to the fight." Such were the manifold sayings of your men, mingled with those of the foe.

sanskrit: viniḥśvasya tataḥ kruddhaḥ kṛpaḥ śāradvato nṛpa pārṣataṃ chādayām āsa niśceṣṭaṃ sarvamarmasu
english: Then, hissing in his wrath, Kṛpa the son of Śaradvat, O king, covered the son of Pṛṣata, now grown motionless, in all his vital parts with arrows.

sanskrit: sa vadhyamānaḥ samare gautamena mahātmanā kartavyaṃ na prajānāti mohitaḥ paramāhave
english: Assailed in the battle by the great-souled descendant of Gautama, he, bewildered in that supreme combat, knew not what was to be done.

sanskrit: tam abravīt tato yantā kaccit kṣemaṃ nu pārṣata īdṛśaṃ vyasanaṃ yuddhe na te dṛṣṭaṃ kadā cana
english: Then his charioteer said to him: "Is all well with you, O son of Pṛṣata? Never before in battle has such a calamity been seen in you."

sanskrit: daivayogāt tu te bāṇā nātaran marmabhedinaḥ preṣitā dvijamukhyena marmāṇy uddiśya sarvaśaḥ
english: "It is by the working of fate that those vital-piercing arrows, loosed by the foremost of the twice-born and aimed at all your vital points, have not made an end of you."
